annotations.text:
A · GROUPED — iOS-native settings grammar, refined.

9 flat cards collapse into 5 labelled groups; every row pushes to a detail screen. Status rides along as trailing values (3 of 5, 7 on, Sep 14) so the summary is free.

Tradeoff: most taps to reach any one setting. Safest, most familiar, least distinctive.

B · STATUS-FIRST — answers "is anything wrong?" before "where is X?"

Billing merges into the identity hero. A 3-tile strip reads security / connections / alerts at a glance, and a real gap (Square + Clover unconnected) gets an amber callout.

Tradeoff: densest of the three, and the health framing can over-dramatize a settings screen on a day when nothing is wrong.

C · EDITORIAL — no boxes at all.

Hairline rules and ember section labels instead of card borders; restaurant name set big in Fraunces. This is the direction Food Cost and Intel already moved to ("whitespace and typography instead of stacking bordered card after bordered card").

Tradeoff: least scannable status; leans hardest on typography discipline holding up as rows get added.

All three are full-scroll renders (not one phone screen) and use the real tokens: Paper #000000, Paper2 #121212, Paper3 #262626, Ink #F0EBE0 / #C4BDB4 / #9E9790, Ember #D4583A / #E8956A, 16px card radius, and the same top ember wash cavnarModuleBackground() paints. Fraunces headlines, Plus Jakarta Sans chrome, Space Grotesk on every number. No fake status bar — the real one renders on top. Rows are 52–54px, above the 44px minimum.

All three assume one change the current screen does not do: Alerts, Connections and Sessions stop being inline walls of toggles and become pushed detail screens.
